Subject: Packaging options for pilot -> production question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — team was impressed with the latency and the prefix caching example. We're trying to map packaging options to our roadmap so we can move the pilot into a constrained production environment. A few things we're trying to clarify:  

- We expect a 4-week pilot at ~120 QPS steady state and two anticipated spikes (1 hour) up to ~380 QPS during onboarding.
- We want to keep the feature gating (NLP-triage and redaction) behind a flag so we can enable/disable without a tier swap.
- Pricing: what's the clean path from pilot (metered) -> committed Reserved/Dedicated? If we commit, are burst credits included?
- Rollback/safe harbor: if we upgrade wrong and need to step back within 30 days, what concessions do you offer?

I've attached a short requirements doc for context (CareSpan_requirements_v1.pdf). Can you outline 2-3 concrete packaging paths + one recommended path for our use case?

Best,
Eli Torres

Hi Eli — great questions, thanks for the requirements doc, that's helpful. I've outlined three pragmatic paths below and added a recommended set based on risk tolerance and predictability.

1) Elastic Pilot (metered -> opt-in commit) — Recommended for teams who want flexibility
   - Start on hosted metered (pay per token / per-embedding) with an Elastic Pilot add-on that reserves a small burst pool.
   - Burst credits: one-time pool equal to 25% of expected monthly token consumption for pilot month.
   - Feature gating: supported via per-route flags; no package change required.
   - Upgrade: convert to Dedicated with a 7-day ramp and optional canary. Proration applies from the day of conversion.

2) Committed Dedicated (predictable throughput) — Recommended for throughput-sensitive prod
   - Commit to a monthly GPU pool (Reserved) with predictable SLOs.
   - Burst: configurable burst capacity (pay-as-you-burst beyond commit). We can include a limited free burst window on close.
   - Step-down: 60-day minimum notice for downward commit adjustments; rollback safe harbor negotiated case-by-case.

3) Hybrid (Reserved baseline + metered overflow)
   - Baseline reserved capacity sized for 120 QPS, overflow metered. Cheaper on average and easier to step-down.

Concession and rollback proposal (what we can offer now):
- One month of burst credits equal to 20% of your committed baseline if you convert to Dedicated within the pilot window.
- 14-day rollback safe harbor: if you downgrade within 14 days we will prorate new charges and offer fee credit for any missed burst for the first 30 days.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Quick alignment call with you + Naomi to choose path, 2) I will draft a mutual action plan and a redline-friendly amendment for the pilot window. Ben and Kimberly are looped for pricing and capacity validation.

If that looks good I can circulate a short MAP and a proposed amendment (pdf) by Monday.

Thanks,

Eli / Naomi — quick follow-up after internal sync with pricing and product:

Confirmed items we will include in the MAP and proposed amendment:
- Elastic Pilot (default path) with a one-month burst credit equal to 20% of committed baseline (non-refundable but usable across pilot month).
- If you elect Dedicated within pilot: a one-time migration credit covering the first 2 weeks of canary capacity.
- Step-down policy: reductions <=30% can be executed with 30 days notice; reductions >30% require 60 days notice.
- Proration: charges are prorated to the day of change; any credits applied in the pilot will be reconciled on the first invoice post-conversion.
- Feature bundling: we will gate advanced redaction and custom reranker behind a per-route entitlement; enabling/disabling requires no tier change.

I've attached a redline-friendly amendment (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) and added a finance-friendly price table to the MAP. If you confirm the Elastic Pilot path I will create a DocuSign for signature and set up a short kickoff (15–20 min) to record the canary window.
